scenes.heading: Geometric reasoning and proof
scenes.sub: Why must it ALWAYS be true?
scenes.say: You know the angles of a triangle add to one hundred and eighty degrees. But how do you know it works for every triangle, even ones nobody has drawn yet? That is what a proof shows.
scenes.caption: You know the angles of a triangle add to 180°. But how do you know it works for every triangle? That is what a proof shows.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A lawyer backs every claim with evidence
scenes.science: A proof backs every step with a reason
scenes.breaks: a jury only needs to be convinced. A proof must leave no doubt at all, for every possible case.
scenes.say: Think of a lawyer in court. Every claim needs evidence, and each piece of evidence leads to the next. A proof works the same way: every step needs a reason. But a proof is even stricter than a court. It must work for every possible case, with no doubt at all.

scenes.heading: The shape of a proof
steps: To prove: where you must end up
Each step: a statement and a reason
Finish with the statement you wanted
scenes.say: Every proof has the same shape. Write what you are given, and what you have to prove. Then build a chain of statements, each with a reason in brackets. Finish when you reach the statement you wanted.

scenes.heading: Proof: vertically opposite angles
notes: Both a and c equal 180 − b
scenes.say: First two crossing lines, then three angles, a, b and c. a plus b is one hundred and eighty, because they are on a straight line. c plus b is also one hundred and eighty. So a and c are both one hundred and eighty minus b, which means a equals c.
scenes.caption: a + b = 180° and c + b = 180° (straight lines). So a and c both equal 180° − b, which means a = c.

scenes.heading: Proof: a triangle adds to 180°
notes: Draw DE through A, parallel to BC
Alternate angles copy b and c up to A
b + a + c = 180° on line DE
scenes.say: Now the triangle, then a construction line through the top corner, parallel to the base. Alternate angles copy angle b and angle c up to the top. There, b, a and c sit together on a straight line, so they add to one hundred and eighty. That works for every triangle.
scenes.caption: Draw a line through A parallel to BC. Alternate angles copy b and c up to A. There b, a and c sit on a straight line, so they add to 180°.

scenes.heading: Proving true vs proving false

right.title: Counterexample
points: Rhombus: equal sides, not a square

scenes.say: To show a claim is true, you need a proof that works for every case. To show a claim is false, you need just one counterexample. A rhombus has four equal sides but is not a square, so that one shape proves the claim false.

points: One counterexample proves a claim false
scenes.say: Quick recap. Every step needs a reason. Letters make a proof work for every case. Equal alternate or corresponding angles prove lines are parallel. And one counterexample is enough to prove a claim false. Now try the practice questions!
